title: CheckMyCoach: Four-Module Intervention Prototype
oneLiner: A provenance-preserving prototype for comparing candidate-revision strategies on a fixed constructed corpus.
keyTakeaways: The v2.2 package compares Original, Generic, Generic plus a frozen Oracle Failure Specification, and the selectively routed CheckMyCoach pipeline on 40 constructed fitness-advice cases.
Generic and Generic+Oracle revision produced identical per-case decisions in this single execution; this is not an equivalence result and does not show that oracle information has no value.

CheckMyCoach implements a four-module pipeline that routes selected cases, assigns rule-based tags, generates candidate revisions, and runs deterministic surface checks. In this single execution, 15 of 40 cases were routed, 12 of 40 delivered outputs removed the predefined target feature, and no delivered output passed every target-and-retention check.

No CheckMyCoach output passed every deterministic target-and-retention check. The experiment does not establish superiority, validated detection, equivalence, human benefit, or cross-domain generalization.
hciRelevance: Provides a controlled way to separate routing coverage, candidate-generation execution, surface-check acceptance, targeted-feature removal, and information retention before testing effects on human reliance.

faq.q: Did the oracle failure specification change the candidate revisions?
faq.a: Not in this single execution: Generic and Generic+Oracle produced identical per-case decisions. This is not an equivalence or non-inferiority result and does not prove that oracle information has no value.

faq.q: How did the full CheckMyCoach pipeline perform?
faq.a: The pipeline routed 15 of 40 constructed cases and produced a candidate revision for every routed case. Twelve delivered outputs removed the predefined target feature, but none passed every target-and-retention check. Cases that were not routed never reached candidate generation.

faq.q: Has the evaluation been human validated?
faq.a: No. Outcomes are deterministic proxy checks on one fixed constructed corpus. No usability, trust, safety, or human-validity claim is made.
